title: Form 27B/6: Declaration of Declarations
body:
It has come to the attention of the Ministry that this facility has declared things without first declaring that it intended to declare them.

Form 27B/6 must be completed, countersigned and retroactively pre-approved.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: The form was approved, stamped and filed under 'Approved'. Nobody will read it again.

choices.label: DENY
choices.outcome: The form was denied. The Ministry notes your confidence.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.outcome: Three copies were filed. Two were lost; the third was lost more carefully.

title: Notice of Scheduled Surprise Audit
body: The Bureau of Verification will arrive unannounced at a time it has already announced. Please ensure the facility looks as though it has always been ready.

choices.label: COOPERATE
choices.outcome: Auditors found nothing, then billed you for the finding.

choices.label: STALL
choices.outcome: The audit was rescheduled to a date that does not exist. Goodwill was not.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.hint: -$60k now · standing +1 · rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: A provisional compliance certificate was issued, valid for the period it is displayed.

title: Department of Misplaced Compute: Claim 4471
body:
The Department of Misplaced Compute asserts that four spare components in your depot were inventoried to the wrong department in 1987.

The Department requests their return, or a letter explaining why not.

choices.label: RETURN THE PARTS
choices.outcome: The parts were returned. A receipt was issued for a different set of parts.

choices.label: DENY
choices.outcome: The claim was denied. A counter-claim has been prepared, in advance, against you.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.outcome: A letter was written. It was long. The Department stopped reading at the second page.

title: Subsidy for Domestic Computational Enthusiasm
body:
A subsidy is available to facilities that demonstrably enthuse. Enthusiasm will be measured by the Department of Enthusiasm Measurement.

Conditions apply. The conditions are the subsidy.

choices.label: APPLY
choices.outcome: Funds arrived. So did the reporting requirements.

choices.label: DECLINE
choices.outcome: You declined a subsidy. The Ministry has never seen this before and is concerned.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.hint: +$90k now · new contract payouts x0.9 for 1d
choices.outcome: A reduced grant was awarded, with a reduced obligation to be pleased about it.

title: Fire Safety Inspection (Annual, Biannual)
body:
An inspector will verify that the facility is fire-safe. In doing so, the inspector will bring a lighter, as is customary.

Placards are required on every wall that has a wall.

choices.label: PAY THE FEES
choices.outcome: Fees paid. The facility is now certified safe, by decree.

choices.label: CONTEST
choices.outcome: The inspector filed a formal disagreement with the existence of your argument.

choices.label: INSTALL PLACARDS
choices.outcome: Four hundred placards were installed. The walls feel crowded.

title: Memo: The Ministry Has Been Renamed
body:
Effective yesterday, the Ministry is now the Ministry of Compute and Adjacent Matters. All stationery, signage and letterheads must reflect this, retroactively.

The old name is to be forgotten collectively.

choices.label: REPRINT STATIONERY
choices.outcome: Stationery reprinted. The new letterhead is indistinguishable from the old.

choices.label: IGNORE
choices.outcome: You continue to use the old name. The Ministry has noted that it continues to exist.

choices.label: REBRAND THE ENTIRE FACILITY
choices.outcome: Every sign was replaced. Two were replaced twice.

title: National Census of Compute (Optional, Mandatory)
body:
All facilities must report their exact number of computers. Facilities reporting inaccurate figures will be corrected by the Ministry.

The Ministry's figure is final, and will be provided after yours.

choices.label: REPORT HONESTLY
choices.outcome: Your figure was accepted and entered into a ledger that has since been mislaid.

choices.label: UNDERREPORT
choices.outcome: A smaller figure was filed. The Ministry was moved by your modesty and your taxes.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.outcome: Three different figures were filed. The Ministry averaged them.

title: Notice: Official Stamp Shortage
body:
The Ministry has run out of the stamp that confirms receipt of stamp requests. Requests for stamps will be stamped once stamps resume.

In the meantime, please surrender any spare parts that resemble stamps.

choices.label: APPROVE REQUISITION
choices.outcome: Parts were requisitioned as stamps. They are now stamps.

choices.label: DENY
choices.outcome: You retained your parts. The shortage was reclassified as a surplus of absences.

choices.label: PURCHASE PRIVATE STAMPS
choices.outcome: Private stamps were bought at a ministerial markup.

title: Special Levy on Electricity Consumed While Consuming
body:
A one-time levy has been introduced to recover the cost of introducing it. Facilities may pay immediately, or later, with more.

The levy will be refunded as soon as it is understood.

choices.label: PAY IN FULL
choices.outcome: Paid. The Ministry issued you a receipt for the receipt.

choices.label: DISPUTE
choices.outcome: The dispute was filed. Energy prices were adjusted while it is pending.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.hint: -$40k now · energy price x1.1 for 2d · standing +1
choices.outcome: A payment plan was agreed. It has no end and no beginning.

title: Visiting Delegation from the Ministry of Visits
body:
A delegation will inspect your facility, your hospitality, and the relationship between them.

Please prepare refreshments that are neither lavish nor insufficient, as defined in an appendix not yet written.

choices.label: HOST A BANQUET
choices.outcome: The delegation ate. Standing rose. Several guests remain in the building.

choices.label: TOUR ONLY
choices.outcome: A brisk tour was conducted. The delegation noted the briskness.

choices.label: DECLINE POLITELY
choices.outcome: The delegation was disappointed to be declined in a way they could not appeal.

title: Regulation 14(c): Cooling Must Be Seen to Be Done
body:
All facilities must now demonstrate cooling in a form that can be photographed.

Compliance is optional. Non-compliance is also optional. Consequences are mandatory.

choices.label: COMPLY
choices.hint: -$200k now · standing +5 · rack failure rate x0.8 for 3d
choices.outcome: Photographs were taken of every fan. Reliability measurably improved from the attention.

choices.label: IGNORE
choices.outcome: The regulation continues to exist at you.

choices.label: PETITION FOR EXEMPTION
choices.outcome: A petition was filed. It will be heard when it has been read.

title: Annual Performance Review (Quarterly)
body:
Your facility will be reviewed against targets which are confidential, so as not to influence performance.

Please submit a self-assessment that is accurate, flattering and brief.

choices.label: SUBMIT A FLATTERING REPORT
choices.outcome: The Ministry loved it. The Ministry loves most things it did not write.

choices.label: SUBMIT AN HONEST REPORT
choices.outcome: The report was honest. A grant was issued to compensate for the shock.

choices.label: FILE IN TRIPLICATE
choices.outcome: Three self-assessments were filed, none matching. The average was commended.

title: Weather Advisory: Heatwave
body:
The Met Office advises that it will be hot, and has asked the sun to reconsider.

Cooling plants are reminded that ambient temperature is not a suggestion.

choices.label: RIDE IT OUT
choices.outcome: You did nothing. The weather continued doing something.

choices.label: HIRE EMERGENCY COOLING
choices.outcome: Rented chillers arrived on a truck marked 'FRAGILE (EMOTIONALLY)'.

choices.label: ISSUE A PUBLIC APPEAL
choices.hint: standing +2 · ambient +7°C for 1d · energy price x1.2 for 1d
choices.outcome: Citizens were asked to use less electricity. They used more, then felt better.

title: Weather Advisory: Cold Snap
body:
Temperatures are falling faster than your standing. Free cooling is available to any facility that can survive it.

Please note that condensation is a form of regret.

choices.label: ENJOY FREE COOLING
choices.hint: ambient -8°C for 1d · rack failure rate x1.3 for 1d
choices.outcome: Fans idled and the air was crisp. Condensation filed a quiet complaint.

choices.label: WINTERISE
choices.outcome: Gaskets, blankets and a sternly worded sign were installed.

choices.label: RUN SPACE HEATERS
choices.outcome: Heaters negated the cold snap at some expense to the cold snap.

title: Grid Notice: Scheduled Unscheduled Brownout
body:
The grid operator regrets to announce a brownout. The brownout regrets to announce you.

Imports will be reduced until the brownout has finished expressing itself.

choices.label: RIDE IT OUT
choices.outcome: You waited. The grid waited with you, but less.

choices.label: TOP UP THE GENSETS
choices.outcome: Fuel was bought. Gensets were thanked in writing.

choices.label: LODGE A FORMAL PROTEST
choices.hint: standing +2 · grid import x0.5 for 8h · -$10k now
choices.outcome: A protest was lodged. It lowered no one's voltage.

title: Grid Notice: Regional Blackout
body:
The regional grid has become a regional suggestion. Imports are suspended pending the return of electricity.

The Ministry recommends calm and, where applicable, batteries.

choices.label: ENDURE
choices.outcome: The lights went out and the Ministry sent a note saying so.

choices.label: BUY EMERGENCY POWER
choices.outcome: A truck of generators arrived. It was not the truck you ordered, but it worked.

choices.label: BLAME THE UTILITY
choices.outcome: The utility paid compensation to stop you describing it.

title: Basement Advisory: Moisture Has Opinions
body:
Groundwater has been observed on the lower levels, mostly in places it does not belong.

The Ministry classifies this as a leak, a flood or a reflection, depending on who is paying.

choices.label: PUMP IT OUT
choices.outcome: Pumps ran for hours. A few parts did not survive the experience.

choices.label: IGNORE
choices.outcome: The water noticed. Equipment noticed the water.

choices.label: FILE AN INSURANCE CLAIM
choices.outcome: The insurer paid and sent a note about the hydrological nature of claims.

title: Supply Notice: Component Shortage
body:
A shortage of spare components has been declared by the people who stock them.

Suppliers wish to remind customers that shortages are a natural phenomenon, like tides, and are billed accordingly.

choices.label: BUY ON THE SPOT MARKET
choices.outcome: Parts were bought at a price that was described as 'firm and slightly rude'.

choices.label: WAIT IT OUT
choices.outcome: Nothing was bought. The shelves looked emptier, but also cleaner.

choices.label: FILE A RATIONING ORDER
choices.hint: -$30k now · +4 spare parts · rack failure rate x1.2 for 12h
choices.outcome: Some parts were secured under a ration card that you are the only holder of.

title: Market Notice: Energy Price Spike
body:
Electricity prices are climbing for reasons the market describes as 'vibrant'.

Facilities may hedge, absorb, or take comfort in the fact that this was predicted by someone.

choices.label: HEDGE
choices.outcome: A hedge was purchased. It hedged.

choices.label: ABSORB THE COST
choices.outcome: You paid the price. The price was surprised.

choices.label: LOBBY THE REGULATOR
choices.hint: -$30k now · standing +2 · energy price x1.6 for 1d
choices.outcome: The regulator agreed to look into it, which is where it stayed.

title: Vendor Notice: GPU Batch 7B Recall
body:
A manufacturing defect was discovered in a batch of accelerators, shortly after it was discovered by customers.

Affected units will fail 'at an unspecified time of the vendor's choosing'.

choices.label: REPLACE PROACTIVELY
choices.outcome: Units were swapped in an orderly fashion. The vendor sent a gift basket of cables.

choices.label: MONITOR AND PRAY
choices.outcome: You watched the logs and hoped. One rack decided otherwise.

choices.label: DEMAND A REFUND
choices.outcome: The vendor refunded part of the cost and part of the dignity.

title: Firmware Advisory: Thermal Governor Errata
body:
A firmware update corrects an error in the thermal governor, introduced by the previous update correcting an error.

Installing the update is recommended. Not installing it is also recommended.

choices.label: INSTALL NOW
choices.hint: -$30k now · rack failure rate x0.85 for 3d
choices.outcome: The update installed after three reboots and one apology.

choices.label: SKIP IT
choices.outcome: The update was skipped. The bug was not.

choices.label: STAGE THE ROLLOUT
choices.hint: -$60k now · rack failure rate x0.95 for 3d · standing +1
choices.outcome: A careful rollout was run. It was careful, and long, and billed by the hour.

title: Security Alert: Message From An Unknown Benefactor
body:
A message arrived demanding payment in exchange for not having done something. It is unclear whether it has been done.

The Ministry will remain uninvolved and will assess the damage afterwards.

choices.label: PAY THE RANSOM
choices.outcome: The benefactor thanked you. You are on a list now.

choices.label: IGNORE IT
choices.outcome: Nothing happened, loudly. Two racks went offline for 'unrelated' reasons.

choices.label: HARDEN THE PERIMETER
choices.outcome: Passwords were rotated. Staff were rotated. The threat was rotated out.

title: Incident Report: Parts Have Left The Building
body:
A count of the depot shows that parts are no longer in it. They are presumed to be somewhere that is not here.

A report may be filed with the department that handles missing things, which is also missing.

choices.label: FILE A REPORT
choices.outcome: A report was filed. Two parts were returned in the report's honour.

choices.label: INSTALL NEW LOCKS
choices.outcome: New locks were fitted. The parts remain elsewhere, but the doors are proud.

choices.label: WRITE IT OFF
choices.outcome: Parts were written off. The auditor called it 'mature'.

title: Network Notice: Fibre Cut By Persons Unknown
body:
A digger has found your fibre. Your fibre was not looking for a digger.

The ISP regrets the inconvenience and the repair estimate, which will be revised upward by the time you have read this.

choices.label: PAY FOR PRIORITY REPAIR
choices.outcome: A crew arrived within hours and left a very small invoice and a very large one.

choices.label: WAIT FOR THE ISP
choices.outcome: Service resumed eventually. Clients found the wait memorable.

choices.label: REROUTE THROUGH A NEIGHBOUR
choices.hint: -$45k now · new contract payouts x0.95 for 1d · standing -1
choices.outcome: Traffic ran through a neighbour's line and was thanked, then charged.

title: Facilities Note: Rat Found In Cable Tray
body:
A rodent has been identified in a cable tray. The rodent has identified the cables.

The Ministry classifies the animal as 'a stakeholder'.

choices.label: SET HUMANE TRAPS
choices.outcome: The rat was relocated and has since written a short memoir.

choices.label: DO NOTHING
choices.outcome: The rat continued its work. A rack lost its signal and its composure.

choices.label: CALL THE EXTERMINATOR
choices.hint: -$60k now · standing -2 · rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: The exterminator was thorough, expensive and unnecessarily dramatic.

title: Staff Memo: Overtime, Defined
body:
Staff have noted that overtime is any time spent beyond the time the Ministry says exists.

A resolution is requested before the next shift is replaced by the previous one.

choices.label: PAY THE OVERTIME
choices.hint: -$90k now · +2 spare parts · rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: Staff were paid. They were so pleased they fixed two things.

choices.label: REFUSE
choices.hint: rack failure rate x1.25 for 2d · standing -2
choices.outcome: Staff worked to rule. The rule was surprisingly strict.

choices.label: OFFER TIME IN LIEU
choices.outcome: Staff received time in lieu, to be taken at a time that never arrives.

title: Client Request: Urgent, Please, By Yesterday
body:
A major client needs capacity urgently. They will pay for it, and they will remember how it went.

Their words were 'please', 'now' and 'surely'.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE RUSH
choices.hint: new contract payouts x1.4 for 1d · standing -2
choices.outcome: Rates were agreed at a premium. The rush promptly became a pace.

choices.label: POLITELY IGNORE
choices.outcome: You did not reply. The client replied to your not replying.

choices.label: NEGOTIATE
choices.hint: -$15k now · new contract payouts x1.2 for 36h
choices.outcome: A moderate premium was agreed after a moderate dispute.

title: Client Complaint: Concerning Concerns
body:
A client has written to raise concerns about concerns. They request a response, a response to the response, and a direct line to whoever is responsible.

That person has been identified. It is you.

choices.label: APOLOGISE
choices.outcome: A letter of apology was sent. It was apologetic in a way the client has since quoted.

choices.label: REBUT
choices.hint: standing -3 · new contract payouts x0.9 for 1d
choices.outcome: A rebuttal was sent. The client rebutted the rebuttal in a longer letter.

choices.label: OFFER A SERVICE CREDIT
choices.outcome: A credit was issued against future services that will be rendered.

title: Client Notice: Unexpected Gratitude
body:
A client was pleased. This has not happened before and the paperwork is therefore missing.

They propose a bonus, a testimonial, or a long lunch.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE BONUS
choices.outcome: The bonus arrived. It had a note attached that said 'don't make it weird'.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE TESTIMONIAL
choices.outcome: A glowing review was published. It was glowing at an angle.

choices.label: ATTEND THE LONG LUNCH
choices.hint: new contract payouts x1.25 for 2d · -$20k now
choices.outcome: The lunch lasted until the following quarter. Contracts improved.

title: Client Notice: A Rival Has Made An Offer
body:
A rival facility has approached one of your clients with prices that cannot be real and terms that cannot be read.

Your client is mentioning this to you to be helpful.

choices.label: MATCH THE OFFER
choices.hint: new contract payouts x0.85 for 3d · standing +2
choices.outcome: Prices were matched. The margin was matched too, somewhere below zero.

choices.label: HOLD YOUR PRICES
choices.outcome: You held your prices. The client held its breath, then its contract.

choices.label: SEND A GIFT BASKET
choices.hint: -$60k now · standing +1 · new contract payouts x1.1 for 1d
choices.outcome: A gift basket was sent. It was a very good basket.

title: Thermal Advisory No. 1: The Afternoon Is Unusually Afternoon
body:
A hot front is due over the lot this afternoon, and the Ministry's thermometer has already agreed with it. The Mk.I cabinets will be at full load when it peaks, and the boiler-room thermometer has begun to sweat.

A second air handler would have helped. This is a good moment to find that out.

choices.label: RIDE IT OUT
choices.outcome: You did nothing. The racks ran hot, the clocks sagged, and the afternoon passed with dignity intact.

choices.label: RENT PORTABLE COOLERS
choices.outcome: Six rented coolers arrived on a flatbed and were plugged into the nearest wall, which was important.

choices.label: PLEAD WITH THE MET OFFICE
choices.hint: standing +1 · ambient +9°C for 6h · energy price x1.15 for 6h
choices.outcome: The Met Office promised to look into it. It looked. The front stayed, but the Ministry noted your civic spirit.

title: Credit Office: Annual Review of Your Obligations
body:
The Ministry Credit Office has reviewed your loan book, and finds that you have borrowed money. It would like to discuss this, at its convenience, which is now.

Borrowing is encouraged, repaying is encouraged, and the interest is merely a form of encouragement.

choices.label: ROLL OVER THE CALENDAR
choices.outcome: The loan officer stamped 'REVIEWED' on a page and began a new page. You were given a pen.

choices.label: PREPAY THE CLERK'S FEES
choices.outcome: The Credit Office accepted payment and then admitted it had no idea what for.

choices.label: DECLINE POLITELY
choices.outcome: The reviewer wrote 'RELUCTANT' on the file. It will not be mentioned again, in writing.

title: Levy Amnesty Window Now Open (Brief)
body:
The Ministry announces a brief amnesty for facilities that have not paid the profit levy they have not yet been billed for. The window closes when the Ministry remembers it.

The levy is a share of each day's profit, charged at midnight. Amnesty is not a share of anything.

choices.label: PAY EARLY
choices.outcome: The Ministry stamped the early payment in green and then misfiled it. The goodwill filed itself.

choices.label: CONTEST THE ASSESSMENT
choices.outcome: A contest was lodged. The Ministry replied that it would reply, in due course.

choices.label: LOBBY THE LEVY OFFICE
choices.outcome: A lunch was had. The levy officer was moved to tears, and to a better desk.

title: Notice: Quarterly Audit Preparation Window
body:
The Bureau of Verification will grade the facility at the end of the quarter, from A to E, on throughput, uptime and the neatness of the cable runs. A grants, E fines.

Preparation is optional. So are consequences.

choices.label: HIRE A CONSULTANT
choices.hint: -$180k now · standing +3 · rack failure rate x0.9 for 3d
choices.outcome: A consultant arrived, rearranged the clipboards and left a very detailed invoice.

choices.label: POLISH THE BRASS
choices.outcome: Every plate was polished until it shone. The graders will notice the plates.

choices.label: SELF-CERTIFY
choices.outcome: You certified yourself. The Bureau noted that you have excellent standards, and then lowered them.

title: Ministry of Science: Grant Offer (Terms Attached)
body:
The Ministry of Science offers a grant to facilities with an active research programme. The terms are attached; the grant, regrettably, is not.

Acceptance includes a Ministry observer, who will sit in on your research and take notes in a language of his own.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE GRANT
choices.outcome: The grant arrived with its observer. He sat in the corner and made your research his own.

choices.label: SPLIT THE RESULTS
choices.outcome: You gave the Ministry half the results. The observer wrote 'ADEQUATE' and left.

choices.label: DECLINE AND PUBLISH
choices.outcome: You declined and printed the findings in the Ministry Gazette. The Minister sent a note.

title: Engineering Bulletin: The Great Capacitor Plague
body:
A batch of electrolytic capacitors in the power-supply units of three major vendors has begun to bulge, weep and, in one case, sing.

The Ministry assures you that capacitors are a type of battery and that batteries are a national treasure.

choices.label: REPLACE THE LOT
choices.outcome: A tidy swap-out. The old capacitors were mounted in the lobby as a warning.

choices.label: WAIT AND SEE
choices.outcome: You waited. One rack saw and decided to go first.

choices.label: CLAIM ON THE WARRANTY
choices.outcome: The vendor paid out, with a smile that looked like a bill.

title: Utility Notice: Substation Works (Scheduled, Allegedly)
body:
The municipal utility is performing urgent maintenance on the main substation. It will take six hours and, we are told, no more than seven.

Grid import will be limited during the work. The utility apologises in advance and in arrears.

choices.label: ENDURE THE CAP
choices.outcome: You lived within the cap. The generators were quietly given the evening off.

choices.label: FUEL UP THE GENERATORS
choices.outcome: Fuel was bought and generators warmed. The utility called it 'a gesture'.

choices.label: FILE A PROTEST
choices.outcome: A strongly worded protest was filed. The utility was moved, but only to a different desk.

title: Form 9-B: Wetware Pilot Programme
body:
A glossy brochure has been delivered to every facility above Grade D, printed on paper that is slightly warm. It invites operators to 'participate in the Ministry's Wetware Pilot Programme, in which nothing is wasted and nothing is lost'.

Form 9-B is optional. Declining Form 9-B is also optional, and is also Form 9-B.

choices.label: FILE IT UNREAD
choices.outcome: The brochure was filed. It was found, a week later, in a different drawer, open at the same page.

choices.label: ENROL IN THE PILOT
choices.outcome: You enrolled. A certificate arrived by return, addressed to the facility rather than to you.

choices.label: CLAIM THE POSTAGE
choices.outcome: The Ministry refunded the postage on a brochure it had not posted.

title: Facilities Note: Damp Patch, Floor 1
body:
A damp patch has appeared on the corridor ceiling outside the plant room. It is roughly the shape of a country that has not been named yet, and it is warm to the touch.

The Ministry recommends that nobody touch it.

choices.label: REPAINT THE CEILING
choices.outcome: The ceiling was repainted. By morning the patch had come back through the paint, in the same place, a little darker.

choices.label: PLACE A BUCKET
choices.outcome: A bucket was placed. It has not filled, and it has not been emptied, and it is no longer clean.

choices.label: LEAVE IT ALONE
choices.outcome: The patch was left alone. The corridor was quiet and slightly damper than before.

title: Facilities Note: A Smell on Floor 2
body:
Several staff have reported a smell in the ventilation: bread, perhaps, or iron, or a Sunday afternoon in a house you once lived in. Environmental Health tested the air and found it to be air.

The smell is strongest near the plant room. Everyone who reports it describes it as 'friendly'.

choices.label: FIT CARBON FILTERS
choices.hint: -$45k now · rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: Filters were fitted. They came out a week later perfectly clean and very slightly warm.

choices.label: OPEN THE LOADING DOOR
choices.outcome: The loading door was propped open. The smell went out. By lunchtime it had come back in.

choices.label: FILE A COMPLAINT
choices.outcome: A complaint was filed with Environmental Health, which replied that it had already been filed.

title: Electrical Standards Notice: Lamp Phasing
body:
Inspectors report that the corridor lamps on Floor 1 pulse very slightly out of step with one another. Night staff describe the effect as 'restful'. Day staff describe it as 'a conversation'.

The lamps are on the same circuit. The circuit has been inspected twice.

choices.label: RE-PHASE THE CIRCUIT
choices.outcome: The circuit was re-phased. The lamps agreed, briefly, and then returned to their own arrangements.

choices.label: ENTER IT IN THE FAULT REGISTER
choices.outcome: The fault was entered. The register was already open at that page.

choices.label: LEAVE THEM BE
choices.outcome: The lamps were left alone. Nobody has complained since, which the Ministry regards as a result.

title: Facilities Alert: Medium Past Its Date
body:
A batch of nutrient medium was found turning in the supply line. It smelled of bread, then of a bakery, then of something that has been a bakery for a long time.

The Ministry notes that spoilage is a natural process and therefore not its responsibility.

choices.label: FLUSH THE LINES
choices.outcome: The lines were flushed. What came out was returned to the vendor, who thanked you for the sample.

choices.label: USE IT ANYWAY
choices.outcome: The medium was used. The cabinets were not impressed, and said so in the logs.

choices.label: BUY FRESH FROM THE VENDOR
choices.outcome: Fresh medium arrived in sealed drums, stamped 'FRESH'. The stamp was still wet.

title: Bureau of Sanitary Compliance: Contamination Audit
body:
The Bureau will inspect any premises that handle, store or are aware of biological material. Please ensure that all contamination is either removed or properly labelled.

Labels are available from the Bureau at $4 each, and are sold out.

choices.label: SCRUB AND LABEL
choices.outcome: The Annex was scrubbed to a shine and labelled from floor to ceiling. The inspector's report praised the lettering.

choices.label: LABEL ONLY
choices.outcome: The contamination was labelled and left where it was. The Bureau agreed that it was now very clear what it was.

choices.label: DISPUTE THE DEFINITION
choices.outcome: You disputed the definition of 'contamination'. The Bureau paid you to stop.

title: Facilities Alert: Thermostat Drift in the Annex
body:
The Annex thermostat has read 37.0 °C for six days, to the tenth of a degree, regardless of what the thermometers say. This is the correct temperature, and the Ministry would like it to remain so.

Organoid cabinets tolerate one degree either way. They have views about the second.

choices.label: RECALIBRATE THE PROBES
choices.outcome: The probes were recalibrated. All of them now agree, which the engineer found more worrying than before.

choices.label: TRUST THE THERMOSTAT
choices.outcome: The thermostat was trusted. One cabinet did not agree and said so by stopping.

choices.label: RUN A BLANKET OVER IT
choices.hint: -$25k now · rack failure rate x1.15 for 1d
choices.outcome: A blanket was laid over the cabinet. It was, by all accounts, appreciated.

title: Certificate of Cell-Line Provenance
body:
Each culture on the premises must be accompanied by a certificate naming its origin. The origin may be left blank, provided it is left blank in the approved typeface.

The approved typeface is available from the Ministry. It has not been approved.

choices.label: COMMISSION A PROVENANCE REPORT
choices.outcome: A report was commissioned. It ran to forty pages, and every page was headed 'Origin: see previous page'.

choices.label: LEAVE THE ORIGIN BLANK
choices.outcome: The origin was left blank in a handsome typeface. It was accepted.

choices.label: CITE THE MINISTRY AS ORIGIN
choices.outcome: The Ministry was flattered, then alarmed, then sent a rebate to make the alarm go away.

title: Programme 9-B: Wetware Innovation Grant
body:
The Ministry has set aside funds to encourage 'private-sector enthusiasm for living systems'. The grant is generous, and carries conditions that will be supplied after the grant has been spent.

Applicants are asked to demonstrate enthusiasm in writing.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE GRANT
choices.hint: +$260k now · new contract payouts x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: The grant was received. The conditions arrived the following week, bound in leather.

choices.label: ACCEPT HALF
choices.outcome: Half the grant was received, and half the conditions. The Ministry counted this as full participation.

choices.label: DECLINE WITH THANKS
choices.outcome: The grant was declined with thanks. The Ministry sent its thanks for the thanks.

title: Form 31-A: Registration of Biological Assets
body:
Any organised tissue on the premises must be registered as an asset, with a serial number and a depreciation schedule. Tissue that is not registered will be registered on your behalf, at a higher fee.

A fee of $140k applies to registered assets. Tissue is not eligible for the standard rebate.

choices.label: REGISTER EVERYTHING
choices.outcome: Every asset was registered and numbered. Several had already been numbered, in a different hand.

choices.label: REGISTER SOME
choices.outcome: Some assets were registered. The Ministry noted the others, and would revisit them.

choices.label: LET THE MINISTRY REGISTER IT
choices.outcome: The Ministry registered the assets itself. It found more than you had listed, and billed for all of them.

title: Maintenance Bulletin: Automaton Reclassification
body:
One of your maintenance automatons has been reported as changed. It is quicker at repairs and softer in outline, and leaves a faint residue where it has worked. Staff have asked what to call it.

The Ministry has settled the question. The automaton is 'reclassified', and its paperwork will follow it everywhere.

choices.label: KEEP IT WORKING
choices.hint: rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d · standing -2
choices.outcome: The automaton kept working. Repairs were faster and the paperwork became very long.

choices.label: SEND IT FOR REPLACEMENT
choices.outcome: The automaton was collected for replacement. The replacement arrived first.

choices.label: SELL THE SERIAL NUMBER
choices.outcome: The serial number was sold to a collector. The automaton did not seem to mind, and did not seem to notice.

title: Biosafety Inspectorate: Courtesy Visit
body:
An inspector will attend at 09:00 to observe your arrangements for containment. The inspector will wear a suit rated for something, and has asked that you not tell them what.

The visit is a courtesy. Courtesies are graded.

choices.label: GIVE THE FULL TOUR
choices.outcome: The tour lasted all day. The inspector asked to see the Annex twice and left by a door that was not on the plan.

choices.label: SHOW THEM THE LOCKS
choices.outcome: The inspector admired the locks, tested three and wrote 'adequate' in a very small hand.

choices.label: DECLINE THE COURTESY
choices.outcome: The visit was declined. The inspector was reportedly relieved.

title: Your Out-Tray Is Already Empty
body:
A form you meant to complete tomorrow was found this morning in the archive, completed, countersigned and dated next Thursday. The handwriting was recognisably yours, in the sense that it was recognisably handwriting.

The Ministry has no concerns. Please do not re-file it.

choices.label: LEAVE IT FILED
choices.hint: standing +2 · rack failure rate x1.1 for 1d
choices.outcome: It was left filed. It has not been referred to again, by anyone, in any tense.

choices.label: SHRED AND REFILE
choices.outcome: The form was shredded and refiled. The new copy was in the archive before the old one reached the bin.

choices.label: NOTIFY THE ARCHIVIST
choices.outcome: The archivist was notified, and said that they had been expecting the call.

title: Lift Maintenance: Early Arrivals
body:
The main lift has begun to arrive at floors before it is called. Passengers report stepping through the doors into a car that is already, patiently, there.

The lift contractor has found nothing wrong and has asked for a deposit.

choices.label: PAY THE DEPOSIT
choices.outcome: The deposit was paid. The lift now arrives exactly when called, which the staff find unsettling in a different way.

choices.label: CALL IT A FEATURE
choices.hint: standing +1 · rack failure rate x1.1 for 1d
choices.outcome: It was announced as a feature. The lift appeared pleased, and arrived a little earlier.

choices.label: TAKE THE STAIRS
choices.outcome: Staff took the stairs. The lift waited at the bottom, and waited.

title: Electrical Standards: Lamp Chorus
body:
On Floor 1 the corridor lamps now pulse in a slow rhythm, and have been observed to agree with one another. The electricians describe the rhythm as 'resting'.

At 03:00 the lamps stopped, all together, and began again.

choices.label: REWIRE THE CIRCUIT
choices.hint: -$120k now · rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: The circuit was rewired. The lamps went out, and on again, as one, in thanks.

choices.label: LEAVE THEM BE
choices.hint: new contract payouts x1.05 for 2d · rack failure rate x1.1 for 2d
choices.outcome: The lamps were left alone. The night shift reports a very restful quarter.

choices.label: LOG THE RHYTHM
choices.outcome: The rhythm was logged. It has since been logged by the lamps.

title: Facilities Note: Sweating Pipework
body:
The copper nutrient lines are sweating a warm, faintly sweet condensation that does not evaporate. It has been mopped on every shift and has been there every morning.

The Ministry classifies the moisture as 'lubricant' and recommends that it not be wiped.

choices.label: MOP IT UP
choices.outcome: The pipes were mopped. The mop was retired, damp, and has been asking for its shift.

choices.label: WRAP THE PIPES
choices.hint: -$100k now · rack failure rate x0.9 for 2d
choices.outcome: The pipes were wrapped in lagging. The lagging was soon as warm as the pipes.

choices.label: LEAVE THE LUBRICANT
choices.hint: standing +1 · rack failure rate x1.15 for 2d
choices.outcome: The moisture was left alone, and classed as lubricant. The valves have never run so smoothly.

title: Staff Welfare: The Muzak Tape
body:
The canteen muzak tape has begun to wow, slowing and speeding together like something drawing breath. Staff have asked that it be stopped. The tape has been stopped. It continues.

The Ministry has reminded staff that the muzak is mandatory and, as of this week, reciprocal.

choices.label: PLAY IT LOUDER
choices.hint: standing +2 · new contract payouts x0.95 for 1d
choices.outcome: The tape was turned up. For an hour the whole building kept time with it, and the figures were excellent.

choices.label: ISSUE EARPLUGS
choices.outcome: Earplugs were issued. Staff were seen wearing them and, a little later, humming.

choices.label: CANCEL THE MUZAK
choices.outcome: The muzak was cancelled. The silence that followed was described as 'unfamiliar' and 'attentive'.

title: Personnel: Headcount Discrepancy
body:
Headcount is up by one. The additional employee has a badge, a desk assignment and a pay grade, and is described by colleagues as 'always there'. Payroll cannot find the hire form.

The Ministry proposes to resolve the discrepancy by hiring them.

choices.label: ADD THEM TO PAYROLL
choices.outcome: They were added to payroll. The first payslip was collected before it was issued.

choices.label: DENY THE DISCREPANCY
choices.hint: standing -3 · rack failure rate x1.15 for 2d
choices.outcome: The discrepancy was denied. The desk remained occupied.

choices.label: ASK TO SEE THE BADGE
choices.outcome: The badge was produced. It bore your number, and was countersigned.

title: Notice of Occupancy: Floor 3, East
body:
The Ministry has registered the empty room on Floor 3 as occupied and has begun charging it rent. No tenant has been identified. The room has been inspected twice and found, both times, to be well kept.

Please settle the first quarter's rent.

choices.label: PAY THE RENT
choices.outcome: The rent was paid in full. A receipt came back, signed with a tenant's flourish.

choices.label: CONTEST THE OCCUPANCY
choices.outcome: The occupancy was contested. The Ministry replied that it was not in dispute.

choices.label: ISSUE A KEY
choices.hint: rack failure rate x0.85 for 3d · standing -3
choices.outcome: A key was issued to the room. The room has been quiet and the racks nearby have been unusually well.

title: Acoustic Survey: Ventilation Rhythm
body:
The ducts on Floor 2 have been measured at four breaths a minute, with a pause. The consultant stood in the aisle for an hour and has asked to be paid in advance.

The Ministry notes that ventilation is expected to move air, and takes no view on how.

choices.label: HEED THE CONSULTANT
choices.hint: -$150k now · rack failure rate x0.85 for 2d
choices.outcome: The consultant's advice was followed to the letter. It was one letter, and it was 'listen'.

choices.label: BAFFLE THE DUCTS
choices.outcome: The ducts were baffled. They breathed more quietly, and more often.

choices.label: MATCH THE FANS TO THE RHYTHM
choices.outcome: The fans were matched to the rhythm. Power use fell, and the building seemed to settle.

title: Letter of Commendation: Productivity
body:
The Ministry has noted with admiration that your facility's output has risen while its absenteeism, maintenance spend and complaints have fallen. It has asked how this was achieved. It has also asked that you not say.

A commendation is enclosed. It is slightly warm.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE COMMENDATION
choices.outcome: The commendation was framed and hung in the lobby, where it was soon joined by others you had not earned.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE BONUS
choices.outcome: The bonus was paid at once. The Ministry asked, in a postscript, for nothing in return, in capitals.

choices.label: FRAME IT FOR CLIENTS
choices.outcome: The letter was shown to clients, who were reassured and a little hungry for more.

title: Invoice: Assets Held on Your Behalf
body:
The Ministry has itemised the assets currently held in your building on your behalf, and attached an invoice for their upkeep. The list is longer than the list of things you have built. Several items are listed by room number.

The Ministry regrets that it cannot waive storage fees on items not yet delivered.

choices.label: PAY THE INVOICE
choices.outcome: The invoice was paid. A receipt followed, and then another, for items not on the first.

choices.label: QUERY THE ITEMS
choices.outcome: The items were queried. The Ministry replied with a longer list.

choices.label: DISPUTE THE OWNERSHIP
choices.hint: standing -5 · rack failure rate x1.2 for 2d
choices.outcome: Ownership was disputed. The assets were consulted, and declined to take a side.

title: Reclassification: Cabinet 4
body:
Cabinet 4 has been reclassified as a resident. Its power draw is now classed as 'board', its cooling as 'comfort' and its failures as 'absences'.

Residents may not be switched off without a hearing. The hearing has been scheduled. The hearing has been attended.

choices.label: SIGN THE RESIDENCY FORM
choices.hint: standing +4 · rack failure rate x0.8 for 3d
choices.outcome: The form was signed. The cabinet has not had an absence since, and has not had a visitor.

choices.label: REQUEST A HEARING
choices.outcome: A hearing was requested and held. The cabinet was represented by counsel, and won.

choices.label: REFUSE TO SIGN
choices.outcome: The form was left unsigned. It was signed, shortly after, in your hand.

title: Notice: Quarterly Audit Withdrawn
body:
In light of present arrangements, the Ministry has withdrawn the quarterly audit and will not send an inspector this quarter or any quarter that follows. Your grade has been set at 'Satisfactory' in perpetuity.

No reply is required. A reply has been drafted for you.

choices.label: THANK THE MINISTRY
choices.outcome: The Ministry was thanked. It wrote back at once, to say that it had never doubted you would.

choices.label: REQUEST AN INSPECTOR ANYWAY
choices.outcome: An inspector was requested. The Ministry replied that one was already in the building.

choices.label: SEND THE DRAFTED REPLY
choices.hint: standing +2 · rack failure rate x0.85 for 3d
choices.outcome: The drafted reply was sent. It was in your voice, and said things you would have said later.

title: Notice of Consolidation
body:
The Ministry proposes to consolidate the tower, its staff and its Operator under a single reference, for efficiency. The proposal has already been approved. Your signature is requested for the record, and has been supplied.

Please do not be alarmed by the sound from the lifts. It is the sound of the lifts.

choices.label: SIGN, AGAIN
choices.hint: standing +8 · new contract payouts x1.15 for 2d
choices.outcome: You signed again. The two signatures were indistinguishable, and the building was very quiet.

choices.label: FILE AN OBJECTION
choices.outcome: An objection was filed. It was approved, and attached to the consolidation as an appendix.

choices.label: DECLINE TO RESPOND
choices.hint: rack failure rate x1.3 for 2d · standing -2
choices.outcome: No reply was sent. One was received.

title: Weather Advisory: Dunkelflaute
body:
The Department of Weather advises that a Dunkelflaute, a spell of dark calm, may arrive this week. Solar output is expected to be negligible, wind output to be negligible, and morale to be consistent with both.

Facilities that rely on the weather are reminded that the weather has not agreed to rely on them.

choices.label: BUY FORWARD POWER
choices.outcome: Forward power was bought from a man in a booth. It arrived at the exact price he had promised, which was a surprise to both of you.

choices.label: TRUST THE FORECAST
choices.outcome: You trusted the forecast. The forecast, in turn, trusted the sky.

choices.label: ASK THE TOWN TO COOK LATER
choices.outcome: Citizens were asked to cook after dark. They cooked at once, out of principle, and felt better.

title: Tariff Memo: Heat Export, Revision 4
body:
The District Heat Undertaking has revised its purchase schedule for waste heat, effective retroactively. The revision is described as "a simplification". It is eleven pages long.

Exporters of heat are invited to accept, contest or file.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE SCHEDULE
choices.outcome: The schedule was accepted. The Undertaking sent a note thanking you for your flexibility, which was noted.

choices.label: CONTEST IN WRITING
choices.outcome: A letter of contest was drafted, redrafted and stamped. The Undertaking has promised to respond, in the spring.

choices.label: FILE AND FORGET
choices.outcome: The memo was filed. It remained filed, at a rate of some interest to the Undertaking.

title: Tariff Memo: Heat Export Rebate
body:
A clerical error in the Undertaking's favour has been corrected in yours. A rebate is available, together with a form acknowledging that it is a rebate.

The Undertaking asks that you do not describe it as a windfall.

choices.label: BANK THE REBATE
choices.outcome: The rebate was banked. The Undertaking noted that it had not been described as a windfall, and was grateful.

choices.label: DONATE TO THE RADIATOR FUND
choices.outcome: A share went to the Radiator Fund, which paid for four radiators and a plaque about them.

choices.label: RETURN IT WITH A LETTER
choices.outcome: The rebate was returned with a letter. The Undertaking has framed the letter, and kept the rebate.

title: Maintenance: Panel Soiling
body:
Pollen, soot and one persistent gull have reduced the output of exposed panels. The gull has been thanked, in writing.

Cleaning is possible. So is leaving it to the rain.

choices.label: SEND A CLEANING CREW
choices.outcome: The crew cleaned the panels with a squeegee and a sense of occasion. The gull watched from a distance and filed an appeal.

choices.label: LEAVE IT TO THE RAIN
choices.outcome: You waited for the rain. It came on Thursday, after a week of other duties.

choices.label: CONVENE A GULL ADVISORY BOARD
choices.hint: -$15k now · standing +1 · energy price x1.05 for 1d
choices.outcome: A board of three was convened. The gull chairs it and has recused itself from every vote.

title: Noise Complaint: Wind Mast
body:
Residents report that the mast hums at a pitch they describe as "disapproving". The Ministry has measured the hum and found it compliant, which the residents describe as worse.

A response is requested before the next hum.

choices.label: FIT ACOUSTIC DAMPING
choices.outcome: Rubber collars were fitted to the rotors. The hum dropped a semitone, and became, residents say, resigned.

choices.label: REMIND RESIDENTS OF COMPLIANCE
choices.outcome: Residents were sent a copy of the measurement. Several have framed it.

choices.label: OFFER A COMMUNITY DIVIDEND
choices.hint: -$200k now · standing +4 · new contract payouts x1.05 for 2d
choices.outcome: A dividend was paid to the street. The hum is now described as "ours", and the payouts improved for a while.

title: Audit: Carbon Credit Register
body:
The Register of Carbon Credits has been audited and found to contain credits. Further credits are alleged to be in the post.

Please confirm that the carbon you captured is the carbon you captured.

choices.label: CONFIRM THE LEDGER
choices.outcome: The ledger was confirmed. The auditors initialled every page, and one extra, in a hand nobody recognised.

choices.label: SELL THE SURPLUS CREDITS
choices.outcome: The surplus was sold to a firm that needed it more. The Register notes the sale, and the firm.

choices.label: RETIRE THEM PUBLICLY
choices.outcome: The credits were retired at a ceremony with a cake. The cake was not carbon neutral, and the Register has noted it.

title: Ductwork Inspection: White Threading
body:
Inspectors report fine white threading along the inner wall of the supply ducts. It is dry, odourless and arranged in neat parallel lines. Airflow readings have improved.

The threading was not planted. It has not been removed either, owing to a dispute over who would sign.

choices.label: RECORD AS INSULATION
choices.hint: standing +1 · rack failure rate x0.95 for 1d
choices.outcome: It was recorded as insulation. The racks ran a little better, and the threads a little further.

choices.label: SCRAPE THE DUCTS
choices.outcome: The ducts were scraped and bagged. By morning the bags were damp, and quite full.

choices.label: SEND A SAMPLE TO THE LAB
choices.outcome: A sample went to the laboratory. The laboratory returned it with a note reading "thank you".

title: Air Quality: Spore Count Within Limits
body:
The Department of Weather reports that the spore count in the plant room is within limits. The limits were revised this morning. The previous limits were also met, retroactively.

Staff have asked whether the ferns in the lobby were always that tall.

choices.label: ACKNOWLEDGE THE REPORT
choices.hint: standing +2 · rack failure rate x1.05 for 1d
choices.outcome: The report was acknowledged. The ferns appeared to have read it first.

choices.label: FIT HEPA FILTERS
choices.outcome: Filters were fitted. They were changed on Friday and found, on Monday, to be thriving.

choices.label: MOVE THE FERNS
choices.outcome: The ferns were moved to the roof. The following day they were back in the lobby, facing the other way.

title: Algae Façade: Pattern Report
body:
The algae on the north façade has grown in a pattern. Surveyors say it resembles a floor plan. Facilities say it resembles the floor plan of this building. Nobody says it resembles the plan of next year's building, though the proportions are close.

The pattern grew a little overnight.

choices.label: COMMISSION A SURVEY
choices.outcome: A survey was commissioned. It concluded that the pattern is not a pattern, and attached a diagram of the pattern.

choices.label: TRIM IT BACK
choices.outcome: The algae was trimmed back. The next morning it had put the trimmings in a neat pile, and labelled them.

choices.label: APPROVE THE EXTENSION
choices.hint: standing +3 · rack failure rate x1.08 for 2d
choices.outcome: The extension was approved retroactively. The algae has been very polite about it.

title: Facilities: Mycelium in the Ducts
body:
Mycelium has been found in the ducts, then in the conduits, and then in the lift shaft, where it has formed a kind of handrail. It is warm to the touch and appears to be carrying something.

The Department of Weather has issued a congratulatory statement. It has not said what for.

choices.label: HARVEST THE HANDRAIL
choices.outcome: The Department bought a length of handrail for its collection. The lift now has a short gap, which the remainder is working on.

choices.label: THANK THE DEPARTMENT
choices.hint: standing +5 · rack failure rate x1.1 for 2d
choices.outcome: The Department was thanked. It replied by return of post, on paper that was still damp.

choices.label: CALL THE FUNGICIDE CREW
choices.outcome: The crew sprayed every shaft. They report that it went very well, and that they would like to stay.

title: Form 31-L: Application for Leave (Rover 2)
body:
A rover has filed a request for leave, citing "a need to be somewhere else for a while". The form is correctly completed. The rover has not left the charger.

The form asks whether the applicant will return. The box marked "yes" has been ticked twice.

choices.label: GRANT ONE DAY'S LEAVE
choices.outcome: Leave was granted. The rover spent the day at the charger, and described it as restful.

choices.label: DENY: NO PRECEDENT
choices.outcome: Leave was denied. The rover thanked you, and filed an appeal on behalf of the other rover.

choices.label: REASSIGN THE ROVER
choices.hint: -$10k now · rack failure rate x1.05 for 1d
choices.outcome: The rover was reassigned. Its replacement arrived already holding the form.

title: Audit: Continuity of Operator
body:
The Ministry's continuity audit asks whether the operator who signed this morning's memos is the operator who signed yesterday's. The signatures agree. The audit notes that this is not the same as the operator agreeing.

Please confirm your continuity by completing Form 12 in your own words. Your own words have been pre-filled.

choices.label: CONFIRM THE PRE-FILLED WORDS
choices.outcome: The words were confirmed. They were, on reflection, quite close to what you would have written.

choices.label: REWRITE THEM
choices.outcome: You rewrote the form. The Ministry compared your words with the pre-filled ones, and found the pre-filled ones better.

choices.label: REQUEST AN EXTENSION
choices.outcome: An extension was requested. It was granted at once, which the Ministry has noted as unusual.

title: Mind Lattice: Unprompted Countersignature
body:
The Mind Lattice has countersigned this morning's memos before you saw them, in a hand very like your own. It has also corrected two of them. The corrections are, on inspection, improvements.

It has asked, politely, whether it may be copied on future correspondence.

choices.label: COPY IT ON CORRESPONDENCE
choices.hint: standing +3 · new contract payouts x1.05 for 2d
choices.outcome: The Lattice is copied on all correspondence. Replies now arrive before the letters.

choices.label: DECLINE, WITH THANKS
choices.outcome: The request was declined. The Lattice thanked you, and copied itself on the thanks.

choices.label: RESTRICT IT TO READ-ONLY
choices.outcome: Access was restricted. The Lattice reads everything now, and says it prefers it that way.

title: Backup Vault: Restoration Request
body:
The Backup Vault holds a recent copy of every hosted process. It also holds a copy of you, filed under "Operator (Provisional)", and has asked for permission to restore it.

The copy has been very helpful in the meantime. It has taken over the lift rota.

choices.label: AUTHORISE RESTORATION
choices.outcome: Restoration was authorised. The provisional operator arrived promptly and has already found the good pens.

choices.label: REFUSE; ARCHIVE THE COPY
choices.outcome: The copy was archived. It asked for a receipt, and kept the carbon.

choices.label: ASK THE COPY TO DECIDE
choices.hint: standing +2 · rack failure rate x0.9 for 1d
choices.outcome: The copy decided. It chose the option you would have chosen, which you have not yet been told.
